purpose: Difluprednate eye drops are used to treat inflammation and pain in the eye, often after eye surgery. They help reduce swelling, redness, and discomfort in the eye. They can also be used to treat a condition called uveitis, which is inflammation inside the eye.
how_it_works: This medication is a steroid that works by calming down your immune system's response in the eye. It blocks the chemicals in your body that cause swelling and irritation. Think of it like turning down the volume on inflammation so your eye can heal more comfortably.
common_side_effects: You may notice temporary blurry vision right after putting in the drops. Some people experience eye irritation, redness, a feeling like something is in the eye, or increased sensitivity to light. Headache is also possible.
warnings: Using steroid eye drops for a long time can raise the pressure inside your eye, which could lead to glaucoma, so your doctor will monitor this. Long-term use can also increase the risk of cataracts. Do not wear contact lenses while using this medication unless your doctor says it is okay. Tell your doctor if you have any eye infections, since steroids can make infections worse. Do not stop using it suddenly without talking to your doctor.
typical_dosing: For inflammation after eye surgery, the usual dose is 1 drop in the affected eye 4 times a day, starting 24 hours after surgery and continuing for 2 weeks, then tapered as directed by your doctor. For uveitis, dosing may be more frequent at first. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions, as dosing can vary.
